label: Late-episode dip after losses, a1 bias, strongest at GO after a1 S1 u
terms: (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial ;; (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * ep_trial ;; belief_lo * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * table(action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) * ep_trial ;; (prev_reward == 0) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * ep_trial ;; (phase != D1) * table(prev_action, {1: -1, 2: 1}) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_trial
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 5 sits near 1 (mean 0.97) and dips, more and more as the episode goes on (timing alone R^2 0.47). Beyond timing, all effects grow roughly linearly with episode trial (scaling terms by ep_trial raised dev R^2 from 0.41 to 0.47). It drops after an unrewarded previous trial, drops further after two losses in a row, and drops more when the lost trial was an a1 choice. The largest single drop is at GO after a1 S1 u (common unrewarded a1, a model-based switch trial). It is lower when the observer belief favours S1 (belief_lo, graded) and at D2 after an a1 choice, and higher at GO/D2 after a rewarded a2 trial. So low r goes with recent losses and the a1/S1 side; high r goes with rewarded a2/S2. Observed-only, with no value/policy terms: test R^2 beyond timing 0.516 (dev 0.518), against the all-cue ceiling of 0.56 (about 92%) and the all-observed table ceiling of 0.52. The policy-decile table alone gives 0.32, which the observed loss-history and belief terms mostly replace, so dropping model outputs costs little here. Adding a three-loss streak term only reached 0.520. A future reward adds almost nothing (0.01).

issues: The claim that every effect grows 'roughly linearly' with ep_trial is wrong. The effects speed up sharply in the last ~15 trials. Linear scaling gives test R^2 beyond timing 0.516. Scaling every term by (ep_trial + max(ep_trial-85,0)^2/2) instead raises it to 0.589 on test (0.585 dev), which is above the 0.56 'all' additive ceiling. Adding just one late-loss term, (prev_reward==0)*max(ep_trial-80,0)^2, to 7 linear terms gives 0.554. Misses: every worst-fit window is at trials 92-99 during loss streaks, where r is under-predicted by 0.1 to 0.3 (e.g. actual 0.57 vs predicted 0.86 at GO, t94-96).

A D2 effect of the reached state is missing. The profile at D2 by choice x state reads a1S1 -0.022, a1S2 -0.004, a2S1 +0.009, a2S2 +0.017, so state matters as well as action. Adding (phase==D2)*table(state,{1:1,2:-1})*ep_trial raises test from 0.516 to 0.539. The label credits D2 only to 'after an a1 choice'.

The 'rewarded a2 raises r' claim is mostly not about a2. With a2 specificity the term scores 0.539 on test; replacing it with plain (phase!=D1)*(prev_reward==1)*ep_trial scores 0.536. In the profile, GO after a1 S2 r is also positive (+0.009). Dropping the original term costs only 0.013, the smallest drop of the 7.

The claims that do check out (leave-one-out, test): loss term (drop gives 0.457), two-loss streak (0.487), stronger drop after a1 losses (0.486), GO after a1 S1 u (0.488, and the largest raw weight), belief_lo graded (0.493; tanh is no better at 0.517). A three-loss streak adds little (0.520).

A systematic residual cell remains: D1 after a1 S2 r is over-predicted by 0.019. After a rare rewarded a1, r dips at D1 but rises at GO (+0.010 under-predicted). This contradicts the simple 'rewarded means higher r' summary. GO after a2 S1 u is also over-predicted (-0.010).
